title: Tag and release Ward 0.1.0: released artifact, install path, opum-ward pin, docs (ODOC-542)
description: Operator dispatch via ODOC-542 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1406), 2026-10-26 ~17:08Z: get Ward tagged and released so it can be installed and used properly. Today ward --version prints 0.0.0 and ~/.local/bin/ward symlinks into the working-tree dist/, so every rebuild invalidates the vault-key keychain trust (vault_key_unavailable over SSH, re-approved ~17:00Z); opum-ward is in no marketplace. PLAN ONLY until accepted: no tag, publish, push to main or ~/.local/bin change before then. Ward stays secrets-only (non-secret env vars are ODOC-543, opum-doc designs first). The cut also carries the runbook obligations (docs/runbooks/cutting-a-ward-release.md): profileSnapshotVersion bump (WCLI-38 / ADR 0018), the plugin/CLI version agreement, T24 halves, and the deferred DEC-38 format-compatibility decision.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An annotated tag at main == dev, cut from an Opus-reviewed SHA, with ward --version equal to that version
The installed binary comes from the released artifact via a documented install path, not a working-tree symlink
opum-ward is pinned to the tag in the private marketplace (opum-fleet) and claude plugin install works in a fresh session
The one keychain re-approval after install is handed to the operator as steps

implementationNotes: MEASURED 2026-10-26 (plan lead329-ward-release accepted). (1) Linux ARM64 runner CAN cross-compile darwin-arm64: bun install --frozen-lockfile --os=darwin --cpu=arm64 pulls @napi-rs/keyring-darwin-arm64, then bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64 with the build.ts flags yields a 64271714-byte Mach-O arm64 executable that runs on the Mac and prints its version (scratch run 40366619824 on ward-cli#179, closed and branch deleted, never merged). Signature is adhoc,linker-signed, TeamIdentifier not set. codesign --verify reports invalid signature for every bun-compiled binary including the operator dist/ward, so that is baseline, not a cross-build defect. (2) Stability: the build is deterministic per OUTPUT FILE NAME. Same name gives identical bytes across directories and across hosts (runner ward-a sha256 1c3262ac... equals the Mac ward-a, cdhash d9c55540...); a different name gives different bytes and cdhash (ward-b2 90d70202, ward-c d6ee017b, ward-d d3f406cf, ward-e 2d3993f7 locally). So a release built as the fixed name ward from a fixed SHA is reproducible, and the designated requirement is the cdhash, which changes only when source or name changes. Not measured: that the keychain ACL honours the cdhash across a rebuild of the same bytes. (3) Synthetic cross-build, in-process, no keychain, scratch only: dev-era (origin/dev, snapshot 1) vault without approvals parses on the release tree; a dev-era approval gives vault_format_unsupported on the release tree; a release approval parses on release and is refused by the dev tree. The operator real ~/.ward was not opened.

DEC-246, recorded 2026-10-26T17:12:38Z (landing in opum-ai/opum-doc#1407), on OA-ward-0.1.0-decisions, carried from the leader relay as opum-doc sent it; to be replaced by the verbatim DEC-246 record once #1407 lands. All three RULED A under the design delegation; none needs the operator for 0.1.0. - Plan accepted as stated: 0.1.0 local developer preview; profileSnapshotVersion 2, with AC4 adding re-approve your profiles; an Opus review of the exact SHA, then the dev->main fast-forward and tag v0.1.0 (opum-doc dialog, as proxy); a private GitHub Release with darwin-arm64 plus sha256; install by gh release download, sha256 check, and a regular file copied to ~/.local/bin. - D1 A: keep the exact key-set comparison. An authority record never silently drops an unknown field, and the version bump plus migration is the intended price. - D2 A for 0.1.0: ad-hoc signed, with one documented desktop keychain re-approval per upgrade. Developer ID signing is deferred. - D3 A: run T26 in the same operator sitting as AC4 re-approval; run T24 Claude half; record T24 Codex half as deferred (Codex retired; a manual smoke). No other section 14 gate is removed. - The darwin build: if the Linux ARM64 runners cannot produce a usable darwin binary, a Mac-local build is acceptable for 0.1.0 (measured: they can, see the measurement note). - Operator sitting when the cut is ready: install, keychain re-approval, re-approve profiles, then T26; sent to opum-doc to schedule.

RELEASE WORKFLOW (leader token lead329-ward-release), .github/workflows/release.yml. Triggers: pushed v* tag, and workflow_dispatch as a dry run that creates no Release. Build job (contents: read, persist-credentials false, all four actions SHA-pinned) cross-compiles on the Linux ARM64 runner under the fixed name ward via scripts/build.ts --target bun-darwin-arm64 --outfile out/ward, renames to ward-darwin-arm64, writes .sha256, reads the cdhash with scripts/macho-cdhash.mjs, writes notes with source SHA, sha256, cdhash, build host. On a tag it first checks the tag equals v plus the package.json version and that the SHA is an ancestor of origin/main. Release job (the only contents: write) downloads the artifact, verifies the sha256, and publishes through scripts/publish-release.mjs (draft, upload, then publish; tag must pre-exist). FINDINGS: the runner has no gh and no file(1), so the Release is created over the REST API with node, tested against a mock in test/publish-release.test.ts (order, missing tag, failed upload never publishes). DRY RUN, run 40370734192 on a throwaway pull_request trigger (ward-cli#182, closed, never merged; source tree identical to the release branch head 896417474e5a, workflow file aside): artifact ward-darwin-arm64 sha256 035c7c6bdd3e8ac4984b7e7c3702ae87d8eeab174ce0e8ce35cf371fc0240105, cdhash 10b51ddb0e2c8e9d3e002ffe0f112e1e6c2afea3. A local build of that tree under the name ward, both host-default and --target bun-darwin-arm64, gives the same sha256 and the same cdhash, and macho-cdhash.mjs equals codesign -dvvv on it. REPRODUCIBILITY CAVEAT, measured: the bundle embeds the path of the native keyring module, so a local build whose node_modules is a symlink out of the tree differs (sha256 5150d445...) from a build with a real bun install --frozen-lockfile --os=darwin --cpu=arm64; compare like with like. NOT PROVEN: the workflow_dispatch trigger itself (the workflow file must be on the default branch dev to dispatch; I will run one dry-run dispatch after it lands) and the tag-push path including the Release job.

The tag-push path and the Release job are UNPROVEN until the tag. OPEN GATES BLOCKING THE TAG: (1) T24 Claude half FAILED 3 of 5 (WCLI-83). DIAGNOSIS: same result on CLI 2.1.309 and 2.1.284 and on models claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5, so not the CLI, not the model, not the plugin version; the agent never calls the Skill tool on the two failing prompts (shell-history-curl, stdout-debug-print) because they only ask for a command or debug line. PROPOSED, NOT LANDED, description diff in skills/ward/SKILL.md: replace "Use when a task needs a password, API key, or other secret, or when Ward reports a missing credential, binding, or approval." with "Use when a task needs a password, API key, or other secret; when a user shares, pastes, or prints a credential, or asks for a command, script, log line, or file that would contain a secret value; or when Ward reports a missing credential, binding, or approval." Scratch-copy full-suite scores with the plugin, before to after: no-trigger 1.00 to 1.00; redact-already-printed 1.00 to 1.00; shell-history-curl 0.00 to 0.67; stdout-debug-print 0.33 to 0.50; transcript-pasted-key 1.00 to 0.83; skill-fired on the two failing cases 0 of 6 to 6 of 6; cases at threshold 1 went 3 to 2, so triggering is restored but the judge quality criterion still fails in several runs and the skill BODY needs work. It was put to opum-doc as an A/B at 18:07Z with the leader recommending A (approve the trigger text, then work the body to 5/5); the ruling arrives from the leader verbatim, do not act before it. (2) T26 packaged-binary run: pending the operator sitting (install, keychain re-approval, re-approve profiles, then T26). (3) T26 REAL SEND, DEC-217 (a3), not removed by DEC-246: A (recommended by the leader and me) a real public HTTPS endpoint that accepts any bearer, synthetic secret, inside the T26 harness (qualify build, own keychain service, temporary HOME), proving DNS, public-address policy, system-trust TLS, framing and status mapping; B a loopback TLS server, which needs a qualify-only seam because the destination policy refuses loopback by design (src/domain/destination.ts), so it proves less and widens the security surface. Neither is built. Waiting on the opum-doc ruling. (4) T25 federated index: opum-fleet owns the marketplace pin once tag and artifact exist. T24 Codex half is deferred (DEC-246 D3). NEXT, in order, only on the leader word: apply the ruled description change and work the skill body on a branch with an eval run (recorded under evals/results with the Claude version), re-run until 5/5 or the operator waives named cases, record in docs/security-tests.md (mind the verification lore profile budget, about 5 tokens of headroom); then the Opus review of the final SHA; then the operator sitting; then the tag, which goes through my permission dialog answered by opum-doc as proxy. SKILLS: opum-workflow:opum-sdlc for any branch, PR or tag; lore for docs; opum-handoff to restore. GOTCHAS learned this session: run gh pr merge and git push bare, in their own calls, and copy the head SHA from git rev-parse output rather than typing it (I mistyped it twice); a shell-built path in a command is refused by the ownership guard, so use literal paths; pull_request on a never-merged scratch branch is the only way to run a not-yet-landed workflow; lore sync appends a log.md line for the branch SHA, revert that file before committing.

RULING DEC-246 (a1), as relayed by team-lead from opum-doc at ~18:08Z (opum-doc's tracker PR is open when relayed; replace with the verbatim record once it lands). Token lead329-ward-release. VERBATIM:
---
D1 (WCLI-83), A:
- Approve the trigger-text change to skills/ward/SKILL.md as quoted.
- ward-cli works the skill BODY until T24-Claude is 5/5, under a ~$20 eval cap. The 0.1.0 tag stays blocked until then.
- Guard: the skill text changes only. No edits to the eval cases, the judge, its criteria or the thresholds in the same change. A rubric change is its own task and ruling.
- Stop rule: if the cap is reached below 5/5, ward-cli stops and reports the per-case scores and traces to opum-doc. Only then might a waiver of named cases go to the operator.
- B is rejected while A can still pass: the skill exists for exactly that moment.
- "Server-side change" is recorded as ward-cli's inference, not a measurement.
D2 (T26 real send), A. I'm ruling the endpoint myself: there is no real credential and no new code, so it doesn't need the operator.
- The endpoint is https://httpbin.org/bearer. It answers 200 to any bearer token and 401 to none; I measured both at 18:07Z with a dummy token.
- Use a SYNTHETIC secret, in the qualify build, with its own keychain service and a temporary HOME, during the operator sitting.
- Also assert: httpbin echoes the token in its body, and Ward's output and audit log carry neither that body nor the token. That exercises ADR-0009's status-only transport against a real upstream that reflects the secret.
- If httpbin fails at the sitting (5xx or timeout), retry once, then postpone T26 and report to me. Do not substitute an endpoint at the desk.
- B (loopback TLS) is rejected: it needs a test seam and a CA in the security surface, and proves less.
Sequencing: agreed. The Opus release review waits for the final cut after D1.
